title: Fresh Limeade with Mashed Lime Zest and Mint
summary: Lime zest is mashed with sugar and a pinch of salt, dissolved in hot water, mixed with fresh lime juice and strained into a concentrate that is topped with still or soda water over ice.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Peel the zest
steps.text: Peel the zest from the 3 scrubbed limes in strips, leaving the bitter white pith behind. Put the strips in the bowl with the sugar and salt.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Mash firmly with the masher for about 2 minutes until the sugar is wet and very fragrant.

steps.title: Dissolve
steps.text: Pour in the hot water and stir until the sugar dissolves, then leave to cool for about 30 minutes. Meanwhile, juice the limes.

steps.title: Strain and chill
steps.text: Stir the lime juice into the cooled syrup, strain into the jug, pressing on the zest, and chill for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: For each glass, pour 100 ml concentrate over ice, top with 120 ml cold still or soda water, stir and add a mint sprig and a lime wheel.

tips: Roll the limes firmly on the worktop before juicing to get more juice.
The pinch of salt sharpens the lime flavour, as in Indian nimbu pani.
Use soda water for a sparkling limeade.
Add the juice only after the syrup has cooled to keep its fresh flavour.
storage: The concentrate keeps covered in the fridge for up to 2 weeks. Dilute only when serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
